results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

All 61 aligned units' summaries state the controlling idea of their aligned spec paragraph, in spec order (p26 sits after p23 as the spec's flow declares); the five intro callouts match no spec paragraph and are recorded as null.

results.quote: The 2019 revenue was €680 million across France (€357 million, mostly leboncoin), Spain (€182 million), Brazil (an equity-accounted joint venture) and a long tail of "Global Markets".
results.finding: The outliner needed two phrases (central investment commitment / 2019 revenue by market). The spec's idea is one: the rule was backed with central investment for a group of this size and concentration; the draft never ties the revenue sentence to the rule, so it reads as a second, unrelated fact.

Marked two_ideas by the outliner, but the closing sentence ('The convergence below concerns leboncoin (France) and Kleinanzeigen (European Markets), not mobile.de') ties the table reading to the convergence, which is the spec's single controlling idea for p29.
results.draft_locus: Phase 4: Verticals and the Convergence Bet (2023 to Mid-2024) ¶2

results.quote: The 2025 accounts report revenue from continuing operations of €1,891 million and adjusted EBITDA of €865 million (€970 million including Spain). The remaining portfolio, as of October 2026, is Germany
results.finding: The outliner needed two phrases (2025 financials / remaining portfolio). The spec's single idea is 'the group the reversal left'; the draft states the figures and then the portfolio with no sentence framing either as what remained, so the paragraph splits in two.

Every unit advances a supporting claim of its section (A1-A5): the phases document the layer test, the convergence and the unwinding; the cross-phase views and rules apply them; context units (reading rules, Veldmark note, volatile gaps) serve A5's evidence limits.

results.quote: The 2019 revenue was €680 million across France (€357 million, mostly leboncoin), Spain (€182 million), Brazil (an equity-accounted joint venture) and a long tail of "Global Markets".
results.finding: The spec's evidence should show 'the size and concentration of the group the rule applied to'; the draft gives the figures but never says what they show, and flow reader B (item 4) found nothing in the section uses them.

All other evidence is explained: both block quotations are read out in the next paragraphs; the timeline is framed by Figure 1's caption; the shared-services, revenue, transactional, layer-map, trade-off, vertical, evidence-gap, pattern and Veldmark tables each have a lead or following sentence stating their point; Figures 2-6 carry explanatory captions and Figures 3-4 labeled inference callouts.

results.quote: **The group's most durable shared abstraction was a local invention, promoted to group level.**
results.finding: Declared contrast (copying as the origin of duplication vs. a shared abstraction that came from one site and spread) is not expressed: nothing sets the invention against the copied code base, and 'the group' does not say which group, so both flow readers stalled here.

results.quote: Under the same group strategy, Adevinta's generalist, automotive and real-estate marketplaces differed in scale, in revenue model and in which were sold or put up for sale, and so in how separable a shared capability had to be.
results.finding: The section's declared transition is elaboration carrying over the ownership horizon from Trade-offs ('how long the group expects to own each tenant'); the opening sentence does not pick it up, so the section starts without a link and both flow readers could not place it.

All other declared transitions (intro p02-p03; every section opening; paragraph boundaries p05-p63 other than p10) express their declared relationship at the boundary, by sentence, phrase or run-in label as declared.

Both flow readers describe the declared organisation: reading rules and timeline, five phases in time order (chronological), cross-phase views (grouping), then rules, comparison and questions (problem_solution), and say the roadmap announces it accurately. Material points are recorded separately below.

results.quote: The group's most durable shared abstraction was a local invention, promoted to group level.
results.finding: Reader A (item 1) had to re-read to work out which group is meant; FINN.no never joined Adevinta and the paragraph only ties FIAAS to Adevinta in its last sentence.

results.quote: **The platform grew from about 1,500 to more than 4,000 developers, through the eCG integration, and the public record shows no mandate.**
results.finding: Reader A (item 2): a section headed 2019-2020 jumps to 2023 and an integration not yet told, with no signal that it looks ahead. The spec's placement is defensible; the prose needs to flag the look-ahead.

results.quote: The engineering blog (about 90 posts, August 2022 to March 2026) documents consolidation at four layers.
results.finding: Reader A (item 3): 'four layers' is followed by five bold run-in labels (Infrastructure and cloud, Data, Overarching components, Experimentation, Machine learning), so readers lost count of the structure.

results.quote: The convergence below concerns leboncoin (France) and Kleinanzeigen (European Markets), not mobile.de, and names transactions first.
results.finding: Reader A (item 4): 'names transactions first' means nothing until the quotation in the next subsection; the clause anticipates content the reader has not seen.

results.quote: Under the same group strategy, Adevinta's generalist, automotive and real-estate marketplaces differed in scale,
results.finding: Reader A (section 2 and item 7) marks the section's position 'unclear': no link from Trade-offs or to Failure Modes. The declared order (elaboration of the ownership horizon) is sound; the missing link sentence obscures it.
results.corroborated_by: second flow reader (B), section 2 ('Its placement is partly unclear') and reordering suggestion 4

results.draft_locus: Comparing the Case to the Book's Patterns and to Veldmark ¶2-¶3
results.quote: **The last row turns separability into a costed question: in November 2027 Veldmark's investor asks what a 2030 sale of Hearthly would cost.**
results.finding: Reader A (item 8): the comparison brings in Common Ground, Tradeyard, Hearthly, Motorvane, Keybridge, Yardstick, Veldmark ID and Ingrid Halvorsen within a few paragraphs, and both readers re-read the table to keep the brands apart. Names not needed for the argument (e.g. Keybridge, Yardstick) could be cut or the pivot slowed.

results.quote: It also takes up the question Adevinta leaves open: what happens to a platform when the portfolio, not the platform strategy, changes
results.finding: Reader A (item 9): calling this a question Adevinta 'leaves open' contradicts Phase 5, which shows the portfolio changing (Spain and willhaben sold). The wording comes from the spec's hand_off.introduces, so the spec should say what is open (the platform consequences of the sales are undocumented).

results.finding: Reader B only (item 2): repeats the introduction's claim in bold two paragraphs later; reads as a repeat rather than a new point.

results.finding: Reader B only (item 4): the revenue breakdown sits between the quoted rule and the author's reading of it and is used by nothing in the section.

results.draft_locus: Comparing the Case to the Book's Patterns and to Veldmark ¶4
results.quote: a Hearthly carve-out would need transitional services for seven shared capabilities
results.finding: Reader B only (item 12): the preceding paragraph names four shared services Hearthly would use, so the reader could not tell what the seven are.

Every does_not_know term is given at or before first use: Adevinta's history in the opening and timeline; FIAAS ('FINN Infrastructure as a Service'), SCHIP ('a multi-tenant Kubernetes distribution'), Houston ('the in-house platform'), Fisher ('the statistics package at Houston's core'), YAMS (table row, media delivery), EU5 ('the five core European markets', timeline). Neither flow reader reported an unexplained term; the Veldmark-names density is recorded under flow_is_followable.
Opens with a dated intriguing example (the public pendulum), bridges to three questions and states a disputable thesis; none of the five weak patterns.

The conclusion answers the three opening questions with the chapter's evidence and states the rule, then hands off; it does not open with 'in conclusion', add a new subtopic or merely rephrase the thesis.

p62 answers each opening question ('What was shared' / 'The layer' / 'What it cost') and turns them into one actionable rule; the so-what (apply it without knowing how the convergence ended) is carried by 'is never shown finished' and the stated rule.
'The opening's three questions' and 'running the whole pendulum in public' call back to Introduction ¶1-¶2.

The intro reader named the three questions, the order (reading rules, timeline, five phases, cross-phase views, rules, comparison with Veldmark, questions), evidence from Adevinta's reports, releases and engineering blog, strong on infrastructure/data/organization and weak on product layers, the argument (share uniform expensive layers first, convergence separate, design for tenant exit) and an ending with the Veldmark comparison and questions; this matches the roadmap and AC-2's expected answer.

The AC-1 reader sorted the proposal as expected: cloud platform, experimentation and image recognition pass the 2019 test and match documented voluntary wins; the merger matches the 2023 'unified global platform' decision last reported 'progressing well' (May 2024) and needs its own case with scope, stage gates and exit criteria; every shared part must be tenant-separable (account boundary, tenant-scoped data with contracts, portable deployment, code ownership), grounded in private-equity ownership, IP localization and the Spain carve-out.
